tossups.text: In 1974, an unsuccessful two-door electric car produced by Gurgel was named after this structure. A Philip Glass cantata honoring this structure has a first movement titled "Mato Grosso." The Santa Maria Ecological Corridor links the area around this place to national parks centered on a large set of waterfalls. The building of this structure allowed many species formerly restricted to one side of the Guairá Falls to invade the other side after the falls' disappearance. In 2009, storms disrupted the output of this structure, plunging an entire country of nearly seven million into darkness for fifteen minutes. This structure, whose name means "the sounding stone" in the Guarani language, intersects the Paraná River. For 10 points, name this dam shared by Brazil and Paraguay, which produces the most electricity of any dam in the world.

This man succeeded his uncle, Rugila, who supposedly died after being struck by divine lightning. This man wielded the Sword of Mars and his court was visited by the historian Priscus. This ruler's son, Ellac, was killed at the battle of Nedao which ended this man's empire. This victor at the Battle of Utus called off one invasion after Pope Leo I likely bribed him. He probably assassinated his brother Bleda and may have been murdered by his bride, Ildico. Theodoric I died fighting this man's army at a battle where he was defeated by Flavius Aetius. For 10 points name this loser at the battle of the Catalaunian Plains, the leader of the Huns.

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for lung lobes and segments. It plays a key role in the respiratory system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this bronchus-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The bronchus is a key component of the Respiratory system, involved in lung lobes and segments.

tossups.text: this structure is essential for skin cell types. It plays a key role in the integumentary system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this epidermis-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The epidermis is a key component of the Integumentary system, involved in skin cell types.

tossups.text: This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for sensory receptors. It plays a key role in the nervous system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this cranial nerve-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The cranial nerve is a key component of the Nervous system, involved in sensory receptors.

tossups.text: This character laughs at a condemned man who becomes furious when he discovers that the person he's supposed to be executed with has been pardoned. This character causes a stir when he arrives fashionably late to an opera with a beautiful woman whom onlookers refer to as "his Greek." To aid an old benefactor, this character returns a red silk purse left on a mantelpiece to a family who later treat it like a miraculous heirloom. This character writes that "there is no such thing as happiness or misery" in a letter to a young man that concludes "All human wisdom is contained in these two words, wait and hope." This character experiences regret when he discovers he had inadvertently caused the poisoning of Edouard Villefort ("veel-FOR"). This character befriends a supposedly mad priest while wrongfully imprisoned at the Château d'If ("shah-toh DEEF"). For 10 points, name this vengeful title character of a novel by Alexandre Dumas ("dew-MAH").
acceptableAnswers: accept The Count of Monte Cristo

tossups.text: The speaker of this book is given a "reed like unto a rod" and is told to measure the temple of God and the worshippers inside. Some events of this book are set off by the "Lion of Judah." It describes the star Wormwood, which poisons the waters it falls on. Martyrs cry for the "word of God" in this book during the opening of the fifth seal, which is followed by seven trumpets blown by seven angels. Its authorship is attributed to John of Patmos. For 10 points, name this last book of the Bible that describes the end of the world.

A U.S. wide visualization of this practice created by the University of Richmond was mixed with Covid-19 data in the project Not Even Past. Data-based analysis of this practice in Philadelphia led professor Amy Hillier to argue one agency's documents, that often listed "infiltration" in section 1e or 2e, aren't a "smoking gun" for its genesis. An advocacy group focused on ending this practice was founded in the neighbourhood of Austin, Chicago by Shel Trapp and Gale Cincotta. Ending this practice was the main focus of the 1975 HDMA and the 1977 Community Reinvestment Act. The FHA engaged in this practice using an "Underwriting Manual" produced by the New Deal organization HOLC. The name for this practice comes from the use of "residential security maps" that designated some areas "Type D". For 10 points, name this financial practice that discriminated against predominantly black American neighbourhoods when offering home loans.
acceptableAnswers: other answers indicating racial discrimination regarding housing

tossups.text: The dynamic theory of these phenomena models them as systems that include an amphidromic point. The namesake producing force of these phenomena is approximately ten to the seven times smaller than the force of Earth's gravity. A set of partial differential equations that govern these phenomena was developed by Laplace. The equilibrium theory of these phenomena was first proposed in Newton's Principia Mathematica and models the Earth as a geoid. That theory allows for an intuitive description of their spring-neap cycle and their namesake bulge. Most places experience semi-diurnal ones. For 10 points, name these phenomena of which there are typically two "high" and two "low" every day.

Following this years-long event, Chris Baldry thinks he is twenty years old and falls in love with his childhood fling Margaret in a novel by Rebecca West. Vera Brittain's memoir Testament of Youth and Pat Barker's Regeneration trilogy are mostly set during this event. In a novel, Lucrezia seeks the help of Dr. Holmes to assist her husband in the aftermath of this event. Andrew Ramsey's death during this event is described in the "Time Passes" section of To The Lighthouse. Hallucinations about the death of his friend Evans during this conflict lead Septimus Smith to jump out of a window, a decision admired by Clarissa Dalloway. For 10 points, name this conflict, the subject of Siegfried Sassoon's poem "Trench Duty."
acceptableAnswers: prompt on the war before “conflict” is read

tossups.text: The 2016 case Utah v. Strieff upheld the "attenuation" exception to one of this amendment's provisions. Katz v. US redefined the provisions of the amendment, which was found to not apply to students in New Jersey v. TLO. One case concerning this amendment involved the plaintiff using the mail to transport lottery tickets. That case, Weeks v. US, saw the first application of one section of this amendment, and also outlawed the use of "fruit of the poisonous tree." The case Mapp v. Ohio incorporated this amendment's exclusionary rule to the states. For 10 points, name this amendment that prevents unreasonable searches and seizures.

In this city, a pair of "grand" and "small" sister museums replaced a former "Palace of Industry." A park in this city contains a museum built in a former tennis court, as well as a museum of "Decorative Arts." A "Royal Bridge," one of the thirty-seven bridges over this city's central river, separates that park from a different museum in this city with a long glass roof over a central gallery. That museum in this city is housed in a Beaux-Arts (boh-zarr) styled former train station and is named after Orsay. A glass pyramid stands outside a museum in this city which contains the Mona Lisa. For 10 points, name this city that houses the Louvre.

Asserting that "a tub had caught all," the narrator of this story invites three police officers to sit down, believing that no one will discover his reaction to the victim's vulture-like eye. Though the narrator asserts that he is not a madman, he describes the torment of a sound "much as a sound a watch makes when enveloped in cotton." For 10 points-name this story in which the narrator reveals himself by tearing up the planks and revealing the dead body of the old man, to end the beating of the title object.

This director titles a 2021 Mia Hansen-Løve film set on an island where this director shot several films. In Woody Allen's film Manhattan, Mary upsets Isaac by placing this director in her "Academy of the Overrated." A film by this director includes a dream sequence in which a man sees his own body in a coffin after it falls off a hearse; that film stars the director of The Phantom Carriage as an elderly professor. In 2021, HBO remade the miniseries Scenes from a Marriage by this director, who also directed the miniseries Fanny and Alexander. In a film by this director set amid the plague, Max von Sydow ("SEE-dow") plays a knight returning from the Crusades named Antonius Block, who loses a game of chess to Death. For 10 points, Wild Strawberries and The Seventh Seal are films by what Swedish director?

A character in this novel hopes that exile to the Falkland Islands will improve his writing. A crowd in this novel chants "We-want-the whip" before a body is found rotating "like two unhurried compass needles." In this novel, Lenina Crowne and Bernard Marx travel to a Reservation known as Malpais. This novel opens with the Central London Hatchery demonstrating Bokanovsky's Process, which separates human embryos into five castes from alpha to epsilon. In this novel, Linda returns to the World State with her Shakespeare-quoting son John, who is often called "the Savage." For 10 points, the happiness-inducing drug soma is used in what dystopian novel by Aldous Huxley?

An alternate name for this figure is Dipaka, which means "little lamp." In one story about him, during the month of Caitra, his remains were put in cuckoos and black insects among other things. In that story, as related in the Matsya Purana, he claims that krodha follows dvesa and that irsya destroys dhairya. In that same story he was accompanied by Madhu and is called to awaken another god from his meditation following the attacks of the demon Taraka. He is eventually reincarnated as Pradyumna, the son of Rukmini, after having been exposed to Madana, which made him "bodiless," and gave him the epithet Ananga. His banner is marked by the large fish Makara and this deity sometimes rides a parrot. For 10 points, name this husband of Rati, the Hindu god of love.

At the Battle of Vosges, this man defeated the Suebi forces led by Ariovistus. At the Battle of Alesia, he defeated Vercingetorix, as described in his Commentaries on the Gallic War, and, at the Battle of Pharsalus, he defeated Pompey the Great. This man also started the Roman Civil War by crossing the Rubicon. For 10 points, name this Roman statesman who, with Crassus and Pompey, formed the First Triumvirate and was assassinated by Cassius and Brutus on the Ides of March.

The Risch algorithm is used to perform this operation in Mathematica, and Fatou's lemma is an inequality relating limit inferiors and two types of this operation. Richardson extrapolation is used in Romberg's method of performing this operation, and the discrete cosine transform is applied in the Clenshaw-Curtis quadrature for performing this operation. One multiplies by the Jacobian determinant to change variables while performing this operation. Certain types of this operation require the norm of the normal vector and a parameterized function. One may change the order in which this operation is performed by Fubini's theorem, and Stokes's theorem relates the surface and line types of this operation. One method of approximating this operation uses quadratic equations and is named for Simpson. Often approximated by Riemann sums, for 10 points, name this operation that can find the area under a curve and is the counterpart of differentiation.

The Zig Zag Towers are in a city in this country, whose airport is home to a giant yellow teddy bear with its head stuck in a lamp. The planned city of Lusail was created for an event in this country, which also used a stadium made out of 974 shipping containers. Like nearby Bahrain, this country only borders Saudi Arabia. The 2022 World Cup was held in, for 10 points, what small Middle Eastern country with cities like Doha?

According to Nick Cave, this city is where the Bad Seeds were first treated seriously rather than as a "whacky novelty act". A 1983 protest song set to the tune of Chattanooga Choo Choo describes a "special train" to a one part of this city. A solo song ending "It's so cold in Alaska" appears on an album titled for this city; that song is "Caroline Says". Iggy Pop recorded The Idiot and Lust For Life at this city's Hansa Studios, which also saw the recording of Heroes. A 1973 solo album by Lou Reed is named for, for 10 points, what European city that names an album trilogy by David Bowie and whose neighbourhoods include Pankow and Kreuzberg [KROYTZ-bairk]?

parts.text: Name this country whose first Sorry Day celebration in 1998 marked the one-year anniversary of the presentation of the Bringing Them Home report to its parliament.
National Sorry Day is a day of remembrance of poor treatment of these indigenous Australians.

The Bringing Them Home report investigated the state-sponsored practices in which Aboriginal children were forcibly removed from their homes and raised by missions and government institutions; those children were referred to by this name.

bonuses.leadin: Though it is not yet a national holiday, many inhabitants of this country celebrate National Sorry Day in late May. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This Polish-born Zionist was the leader of the Histadrut, a Zionist labor federation, before he became Israel's first prime minister.

This Likudnik prime minister from 1977-1983 was a member of the Irgun prior to the establishment of Israel. As prime minister, he presided over Israel's 1982 invasion of southern Lebanon and negotiated the Camp David Accords, for which he shared a Nobel Peace Prize.
This man led a special forces raid at the Lod International Airport in 1972. This one-time leader of the Labor Party has recently formed the splinter Atzmaut Party.

bonuses.leadin: Identify these prime ministers of Israel, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with parathyroid hormone.
What is the main function of the thyroid in the endocrine system?
Name another component of the endocrine system related to parathyroid hormone.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human endocrine system.

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with cranial nerves.
What is the main function of the cranial nerve in the nervous system?
Name another component of the nervous system related to cranial nerves.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human nervous system.

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with skeletal muscle structure.
What is the main function of the sarcomere in the musculoskeletal system?
Name another component of the musculoskeletal system related to skeletal muscle structure.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human musculoskeletal system.

parts.text: This beverage is traditionally made by distilling raw spirits with juniper berries and other herbs.
Gin is mixed with this fortified wine to make a martini. It gets is name from the German word for wormwood, an ingredient no longer typically found in this drink.
Vermouth, sherry, and Campari are all this sort of beverage served before a meal to stimulate appetite. The term takes its name from the Latin for "to open".

bonuses.leadin: Answer these questions about classy beverages. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Give the name for this state of high spiritual consciousness, a trancelike state which is reached through proper practice of dhyana, or meditation.
Samadhi is the last of this many components of a "path" to salvation in Buddhism.
The Eightfold Path is often symbolized by an eight-spoked "wheel" of this common concept from Indian religions, which roughly translates to "proper way of living."

bonuses.leadin: Focusing using an object allows one to reach the savikalpa form of this state, in which the ego is completely released. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this colony where Andrés Bonifacio's KKK revolutionary society gained traction after the execution of an ilustrado leader in 1896.

Ilustrados were frustrated with traditional Spanish rule with people with this position ruling over towns in namesake "ocracias." The Gomburza affair executed three Filipino priests for campaigning against the rule of people in this position.
de la Torre's reforms included abolishing this punishment. Los Picaos perform this form of self-harm, practitioners of which ironically helped spread the Black Plague while atoning for their sins.

bonuses.leadin: This colony's educated elite were named ilustrados and befriended the reformist governor Carlos María de la Torre. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this human form of transmissible spongiform encephalopathy.
Stanley Pruisner discovered these infectious proteins that cause Creutzfeldt-Jacob. Other diseases they cause include mad cow, scrapie, and kuru.
Abnormally high numbers of beta pleated sheets form in misfolded prions, as opposed to this normal, coiled prion structure.

bonuses.leadin: Dementia, myoclonia, and seizures result from this disease's destruction of nervous tissues in the brain, leading to a characteristic appearance under a microscope. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this short story about Cherokee Sal's child.
This author wrote "The Luck of Roaring Camp" and about the expulsion of four "immoral" people in his story, "The Outcasts of Poker Flat."
Most of Harte's works concern miners in this state, which is also the setting of Raymond Chandler's The Big Sleep.

bonuses.leadin: After getting his finger "rastled" the main protagonist in work exclaims "the damned little cuss!" and Kentuck is later found dying after the North Fork. For ten points each:

parts.text: This man ruled Athens through the first part of the Peloponnesian war before he died of the plague afflicting Athens.
This man was known for reforming Athenian law, and released all enslaved citizens along with many other reforms, being given temporary supreme power.
This benevolent tyrant of Athens was held in high regard, though his son would go paranoid and end the virtual dynasty he started, and his reign saw a flourishing of the arts.

bonuses.leadin: Name some politicians who led Athens, for 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this semiarid region that stretches east to west across an entire continent for over 3500 miles. It includes pastures with scattered baobabs and acacias and is under substantial desertification pressure.
The desert north of the Sahel is this desert, the world's largest, in North Africa.
The more wooded area south of the Sahel is often given this name, translating as "Land of the Blacks." A country with this name includes the Darfur region, a site of ongoing conflict since 2003.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, name these specific climatic regions.

parts.text: This is what novella in which the unnamed Governess suspects that the ghost of her predecessor and her predecessor's lover are haunting the house, where she takes care of Flora and Miles.
The Turn of the Screw is by this American author, who also wrote The Wings of the Dove and The Golden Bowl.
Lord Warburton, Caspar Goodwood, and Gilbert Osmond are among those pursuing Isabel Archer in this Henry James, often considered his masterwork.

bonuses.leadin: In the frame narrative of this work sees the narrator and his friends exchanging ghost stories on Christmas Eve, FTPE:

parts.text: Identify these German brothers who collected and retold various folk tales, such as those of Hansel and Gretel, Sleeping Beauty, and Snow White.

This American author included "The Unicorn in the Garden" in his 1940 collection Fables for Our Time. This author's best-known story recounts the mundane life of a man who experiences several heroic daydreams.
This English author of Nights at the Circus drew inspiration from Charles Perrault's fairy tales in writing her magical realist collection The Bloody Chamber.

bonuses.leadin: This duo's first collection was published in 1812. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this play in which the mayor Anton Antonovich mistakes Khlestakov for the dreaded title figure.

The protagonist of this work is thought to be Captain Koepikin by the postmaster. This novel centers on Pavel Chichikov, who tries to collect the title objects by owning the legal rights of deceased serfs.
This author wrote about an article of clothing owned by Akaky Akakievich in The Overcoat in addition to writing The Inspector General and Dead Souls.

bonuses.leadin: Characters in this play include the country squires Bobchinsky and Dobchinsky, and the central character of this work proposes to Maria. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these objects which, according to an interpretation by Elias Lonnrot, include the Sampo that could produce gold and salt out of thin air in addition to more typical products of this object like flour.
The Sampo is forged by this legendary blacksmith from the Kalevala in an unsuccessful attempt to win the hand of the beautiful daughter of the witch queen Louhi.
One theory hypothesizes that Louhi's land of Pohjola was the land of the Sámi. Unusually shaped examples of these objects called Sieidi are held sacred by the Sámi.

bonuses.leadin: The Aarne-Thompson-Uther tale type 565 classifies tales about magical examples of these objects including the Grottasöngr where two Jotunn slave girls work in one of these objects. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this religion whose Five Pillars include making hajj, or pilgrimage to Mecca, once in one's lifetime.
This sect of Islam, the dominant sect in Iran, considers Ali to be the first caliph, disputing Abu Bakr's claim.
Ali was married to this daughter of Muhammad, who opposed Abu Bakr and Umar and was the namesake of an Egyptian Shi'a dynasty lasting from 909 to 1171 CE.

bonuses.leadin: This religion's central beliefs include giving at least 2.5 percent of one's income to charity, or Zakat. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these types of volcano. They include Mauna Loa and Kilauea ["kil-la-WAY-uh"].
Lava flows from volcanoes form the extrusive kind of this type of rock. The intrusive kind of this rock is formed from magma.
Shield volcanoes can erupt two kinds of lava: a'a ["ah-ah"] and this kind of lava, which is thin and flows more easily than the former.

bonuses.leadin: These structures are formed from low-viscosity lava flows and tend to be low and flat. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this lake in Central Asia, which is now split into six different parts. It lies east of the Caspian Sea.
The damming of the rivers was ordered to increase the production of this cash crop in Uzbekistan. This crop was also produced by slaves in the Southern United States before the civil war.
The Aral Sea bordered Uzbekistan and this largest land-locked country, whose capital had its name changed in 2019 from Astana to Nur-Sultan.

bonuses.leadin: Before the damming of the Amu and Syr Darya rivers, this lake was one of the largest inland lakes in the world. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this social class that came to dominate the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth during the age of Golden Liberty. Many members of the legislative body known as the Sejm ("same") came from this social class.

By declaring "I do not allow it," any member of the Sejm could invoke this heavily-abused right to defeat any measure under consideration, or to dissolve the Sejm and nullify all acts during its session.

The liberum veto was abolished after Poland adopted the first codified document of this type in Europe in 1791, during the reign of Stanisław Poniatowski ("STAH-nee-swoff poh-nya-TOF-ski"), just two years after the United States adopted one in 1789.

bonuses.leadin: The Henrician Articles established the right of this social class to directly elect the king. For 10 points each:
